title: If allies fade when they see the crowd walking away from them, does the robots' tip survive?
lede: allies who convert only when they have watched the crowd walk the other way. With 20% allies, fading at rate c times the share of R in their memory tips more crowds than a constant rate c once robots are 0.10 or more (12/12 vs 10/12 at c = 0.01, robots 0.10; 4/12 vs 0/12 at c = 0.03), but does nothing below 0.05. Stylised
summary: The society-allyfade crowd (200 people, memory 9, error 0.02, 12 seeds, 1500 rounds) with 20% allies who walk the robots' side, comparing a constant fade rate c with a rate c×f, where f is the share of the ally's own memory on the other side. At c = 0.01 and robot share 0.10 all 12 crowds tip with watching allies (about 26 of 40 allies still there) against 10 with constant fading; at c = 0.03 it is 4 against 0 at 0.10 and 12 against 10 at 0.15; at 0.05 robots only 2 of 12 tip at c = 0.01 against 0. The first rounds are the same in both rules (memories start all R, so f = 1), so the gain comes only after the tip begins: allies who watch it stay. Below 0.05 robots, or at c ≥ 0.1, neither rule tips. Stylised: the discouragement rule and its rates are assumed, not measured; simulated walkers only.
